title: Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection - Post-Award Formalities - Protests
subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: What legal mechanism typically automatically pauses the final execution of a contract when a timely, formal complaint is filed by an aggrieved bidder regarding the award decision?
questions.explain: A Stay of Award (or suspension of action) prevents the agency from executing the contract or proceeding with the procurement until the formal vendor protest has been thoroughly investigated and resolved.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: In public procurement, the strict timeline for a vendor to file a formal bid protest (e.g., within 7 days) generally begins when:
options: The Notice of Intent to Award is publicly posted or vendors are formally notified of the decision
questions.explain: While pre-bid protests (challenging specs) must be filed before the bid opens, an award protest timeline strictly starts the moment the agency formally notifies the public/vendors of who they intend to award the contract to.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: To have 'standing' to file a formal legal bid protest against a contract award, the protesting party typically must be:
options: Any taxpayer residing within the agency's jurisdiction
An actual or prospective bidder whose direct economic interest is adversely affected by the award of the contract
A local news reporter covering government spending
A vendor who downloaded the bid but chose not to submit a response
questions.explain: Standing refers to the legal right to initiate a lawsuit or protest. In procurement, only an 'interested party' (an actual bidder who suffered potential economic harm due to a flawed award process) has standing to protest.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection

questions.q: Which of the following scenarios forms a legally valid basis to sustain a formal vendor protest?
options: The protesting vendor feels they are simply a better company than the winner
A mathematical error was made in the agency's official evaluation scoring which, if corrected, makes the protesting vendor the true highest-scoring proposer
The winning vendor is located 500 miles away
The protesting vendor submitted their bid late, but only by two minutes
questions.explain: Protests must be based on objective violations of law, flawed procedures, biases, or material mathematical errors in applying the evaluation criteria, not simply a disagreement with the agency's subjective judgment.
questions.subject: CPPB Domain III: Sourcing & Supplier Selection
